correctness.rationale: PASS applies to repairs/2/RESULT.md, not the original unrestricted assertion about strict instability beyond the upper bound. In the original Finding (line 25), take N=3, blocks (1,2), β=3/4. Then β>β_c=2/3 but the only within-block quotient multiplier of the one-step Jacobian is −1, and the difference multiplier is 1/2. The two-step quotient spectrum {1,1/4} has no unstable multiplier. The repair supplies the exact boundary classification. Independent reconstruction: F(v)=v−νPv+k(Pv)^∘3 with the uniform projection removed by P; block deviations are (ℓ/N)d and −(m/N)d. Their cubic difference has coefficient k(m³+ℓ³)/N³=kD/N²; their contribution to mean drift is kmℓ(ℓ−m)d³/N³. Sign reversal forces kd²D/N²=β and the initial drift sets the unique antipodal mean to −H/2. The two phase Jacobians coincide by evenness of the squared deviations. The within-block zero-sum modes and the difference mode diagonalize the quotient, yielding the squared return multipliers from −1+βN(2ℓ−m)/D, −1+βN(2m−ℓ)/D and −1+2β, with absent singleton modes removed. Writing M and q for larger and smaller block sizes, the M-mode forbids strict contraction at M≥2q and is unstable if M>2q. For M<2q both within-block modes are present and the q-mode first hits +1 at β_c≤1; equality is nonhyperbolic and β>β_c unstable there. For M=2q the M-mode stays at −1; the q-mode, if present, hits +1 at 2/3, and if absent the difference mode first hits +1 at 1. In the stable region contraction on the quotient makes the smooth two-step mean drift summable, giving a common translate. Direct rational substitution gives the five-agent orbit and the stated spectrum, with N=3 ruled out for strict attraction. The frozen checker was inspected but not run; its 65 partitions use β=1/4, so the recorded PASS does not test the instability boundary counterexample. The correction preserves the strict-attraction theorem and proof witnesses.
